description: RAW WATER SYSTEM SCHEMATIC, drawing 108-01-S15-001, sheet 1/1. Fluid-path reading: Both sea-water cooling circuits draw from SEACHEST 001-01 through separate normally-open 2-inch inlet valves and sea-water strainers, then through the port or starboard main cooling seawater pump. Each pump discharge passes its local normally-open discharge valve and flow sensor, then feeds the corresponding MAIN SYSTEM HEAT EXCHANGER 010-01 (port) or 010-02 (starboard). Downstream of each main heat exchanger, raw water discharges through a normally-open 1.5-inch overboard valve to a below-DWL seawater outlet. Each heat-exchanger section has readable isolation/bypass valves: port 017-01 and 017-02 around 010-01, with 019-01 and 019-02 on the heat-exchanger connections; starboard 017-03 and 017-04 around 010-02, with 019-03 and 019-04 on the heat-exchanger connections. HYDRAULIC PUMPS HEAT EXCHANGER 011-01 is a parallel branch between the port circuit headers, isolated by 005-03 and 005-04. PITCH CONTROL HEAT EXCHANGER 012-01 and CPP SEAWATER PUMP 005-05 form the pitch-control branch; 005-01 is shown at the stern-tube-bearing/hundested supply connection and 005-06 isolates the CPP pump outlet. Port and starboard main cooling circuits are linked by a central green cross-over/header fitted with two normally-closed cross-over valves; this allows one side/header to support the other when intentionally opened. A separate flush/fresh-water priming arrangement enters each main-pump suction through normally-closed valve 018-02 (port) and 018-01 (starboard); labels cross-reference the fresh-water supply and dedicated water pump on DWG 108-01-S10-01. SEACHEST 001-01 contains two sea-water strainers with normally-open 3-inch valves at strainer entries, normally-closed top backflush/vent connections, and below-DWL sea-water inlets; branch valves on the sea-chest manifold isolate the port pump suction, flush connection, starboard pump suction, and the lower auxiliary branch. Cathodic galvanic protection unit 009-01 is associated with the sea chest. Port and starboard generator raw-water pumps are package-mounted in the generator coolant circuits. Each receives sea water from the green raw-water header and discharges through an exhaust outlet to the exhaust silencer; each generator branch includes an ANTI-SIPHON MANIFOLD, 015-01 port and 015-02 starboard, with breather routed to the engine-room vent box. The generator coolant-package cross-reference is DWG 108-01-S15-002; exhaust outlet cross-reference is DWG 108-01-440-001; vent-box cross-reference is DWG 108-01-S08-001. Boiler internal heat exchangers are joined by pink coolant/flexible-pipe runs: 80L FWD BOILER at upper right and 80L AFT BOILER at left-middle. Lower auxiliary raw-water branches: AIRCON SYSTEM REF. DWG 108-01-S90-001 is supplied through SEAWATER STRAINER 003-02, with normally-closed top service/breather valve and below-DWL inlet/outlet isolation valves; WATERMAKER UNITS REF. DWG 108-01-S10-001 is similarly supplied through SEAWATER STRAINER 003-03. Flow arrows show sea chest/inlet or fresh-water priming source toward pumps, then heat exchangers/consumers, and finally overboard/outlet. Printed performance data: STBD/PORT GENERATOR RAW WATER PUMP—Sherwood P2709-01, 193 l/min at 2500 rpm. MAIN COOLING CIRCUIT SEAWATER PUMPS—Grundfos CME 10-1 A-R-G-V, 200 l/min, 1.1 kW. CONTROLLABLE PITCH SEAWATER PUMP—Calpeda BCM 20/A, 80 l/min, 0.37 kW. Pitch-control note: minimum flow 22.5 l/min; max pressure 1.2 bars (0.6–0.7 bar is sufficient); suitable pressure/flow regulators plus gauges may be required. Drawing-specific notes state that thru-hull valves are detailed separately in DWG 108-01-S40-002, Thru-Hull Fittings Below & Near DWL; refer to DWG 108-01-S15-002 Cooling Water System Schematic; quick couplings on main heat exchangers allow flushing of seawater circuit to remove fouling.
